title.zh: 卷299 列傳八十六 马会伯 马际伯 马见伯 觌伯 路振杨 韩良辅 韩良卿 韩勋 杨天纵 王郡 宋爱
title.en: Volume 299 Biographies 86: Ma Huibo, Ma Jibo, Ma Jianbo, Di Bo, Lu Zhenyang, Han Liangfu, Han Liangqing, Han Xun, Yang Tianzong, Wang Jun, Song Ai
title.raw: 卷299 列傳八十六 马会伯 马际伯 马见伯 觌伯 路振杨 韩良辅 韩良卿 韩勋 杨天纵 王郡 宋爱

sentences.zh: 列傳八十六

translations.literal: Biographies eighty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 86

sentences.zh: 馬會伯從兄際伯際伯弟見伯覿伯路振揚韓良輔弟良卿子勳

translations.literal: Ma Huibo; his elder cousin Jibo; Jibo's younger brother Jianbo; Dibo; Lu Zhenyang; Han Liangfu; Liangfu's younger brother Liangqing; Liangqing's son Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Huibo; his elder cousin Ma Jibo; Ma Jibo's younger brother Ma Jianbo; Di Bo; Lu Zhenyang; Han Liangfu; Han Liangfu's younger brother Han Liangqing; Han Liangqing's son Han Xun

sentences.zh: 楊天縱王郡宋愛

translations.literal: Yang Tianzong; Wang Jun; Song Ai.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tianzong; Wang Jun; Song Ai

sentences.zh: 馬會伯，陝西寧夏人。

translations.literal: Ma Huibo was a native of Ningxia in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Huibo was from Ningxia in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十九年一甲一名武進士，授頭等侍衛。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year of Kangxi he took first place in the first class of the military jinshi examination and was appointed a first-rank bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year of the Kangxi reign (1700), he placed first in the first class of the military jinshi examination and was appointed a first-rank imperial bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，授直隸昌平參將，累遷雲南永北總兵。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he was made garrison commander of Changping in Zhili, and was promoted in stages to commander-in-chief at Yongbei in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year (1706) he was appointed garrison commander of Changping in Zhili, and rose in stages to commander-in-chief at Yongbei in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，師入西藏，命會伯與總兵趙坤率綠旗兵會都統法喇從征。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year, when the army entered Tibet, Huibo was ordered to join the campaign with Commander Zhao Kun leading Green Standard troops to unite with Commander-in-Chief Fa La.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-ninth year (1720), when troops marched into Tibet, Huibo was ordered to join the campaign with Commander Zhao Kun, leading Green Standard troops to rendezvous with Commander-in-Chief Fa La.

sentences.zh: 西藏定，敘功，加左都督。

translations.literal: When Tibet was pacified, merit was recorded and he was advanced to Left Commissioner-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After Tibet was pacified, his service was rewarded with promotion to Left Commissioner-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，入覲，世宗書榜賚焉，曰「有儒將風」，並賜貂冠、孔雀翎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he came to court; the Shizong Emperor wrote an inscription on a placard and bestowed it on him, saying "He has the bearing of a scholar-general," and also granted him a sable cap and peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yongzheng reign (1723) he presented himself at court. The Yongzheng Emperor inscribed a placard for him reading "He has the bearing of a scholar-general," and also granted him a sable cap and peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 其從弟覿伯，以山西大同總兵率師駐山丹衛，命會伯代鎮，賜白金五百。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Dibo, as commander-in-chief at Datong in Shanxi, was leading troops stationed at Shandanwei; Huibo was ordered to replace him in command and was granted five hundred taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: His younger cousin Di Bo, serving as commander-in-chief at Datong in Shanxi, had been leading troops stationed at Shandanwei. Huibo was ordered to take over the command, and was granted five hundred taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 二年，還鎮永北。

translations.literal: In the second year he returned to his post at Yongbei.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (1724) he returned to his command at Yongbei.

sentences.zh: 三年，擢貴州提督，疏言：「貴州土瘠兵貧，臣捐穀千石，所屬四營將備捐千石，貯以濟兵。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to provincial military commander of Guizhou and memorialized: "Guizhou's soil is poor and the troops impoverished; your servant donates a thousand piculs of grain, and the four battalions' officers and deputies under him donate a thousand piculs, to be stored for relieving the troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1725) he was promoted to provincial military commander of Guizhou and memorialized: "Guizhou's land is poor and the troops are impoverished. Your servant donates a thousand piculs of grain, and the officers and deputies of the four battalions under my command donate another thousand, to be stored for the relief of the troops.

sentences.zh: 來歲續捐增貯。」

translations.literal: Next year donations will continue to increase the stores."
translations.idiomatic: Next year I shall continue donating to increase the stores."

sentences.zh: 上善之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 初，廣順屬長寨仲苗最悍，總督高其倬奏移兵設汛。

translations.literal: Earlier, among the Zhong Miao of Changzhai under Guangshun, the most fierce had been subdued; Governor-General Gao Qisuo memorialized to shift troops and establish garrison posts.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Zhong Miao of Changzhai under Guangshun had been the most fierce; Governor-General Gao Qisuo had memorialized to redeploy troops and establish garrison posts.

sentences.zh: 是歲，建營房，仲苗出阻。

translations.literal: That year, as barracks were being built, the Zhong Miao came out to obstruct.
translations.idiomatic: That year, as barracks were being built, the Zhong Miao came out to obstruct the work.

sentences.zh: 會伯會總兵石禮哈率兵捕治，得其酋阿革、阿紀及川販為主謀者李奇，悉誅之，餘眾詣軍前聽命。

translations.literal: Huibo joined Commander Shi Liha in leading troops to capture and punish them; they seized the chieftains Age and Aji and Li Qi, a Sichuan trader who had been the chief plotter, and executed them all; the rest came before the army to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Huibo joined Commander Shi Liha in leading troops to suppress them. They captured the chieftains Age and Aji, along with Li Qi, a Sichuan trader who had been the chief instigator, and executed them all. The remaining tribesmen came before the army to submit.

sentences.zh: 會伯复赴宗角、者貢、谷隆關、羊城諸地督建營房，得旨嘉獎。

translations.literal: Huibo again went to Zongjiao, Zhegong, Gulongguan, Yangcheng'ao and other places to supervise the building of barracks, and received an edict of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Huibo then went in person to Zongjiao, Zhegong, Gulongguan, Yangcheng'ao, and other sites to supervise construction of barracks, for which he received an edict of commendation.

sentences.zh: 四年，調甘肅，未至，又調署四川，旋授四川巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Gansu; before he arrived he was again transferred to act in Sichuan, and soon after was appointed governor of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1726) he was transferred to Gansu, but before he could take up the post he was reassigned to act in Sichuan, and soon afterward was appointed governor of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 五年，疏劾按察使程如絲營私網利，遣侍郎黃炳按鞫得實，論罪如律。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he memorialized impeaching Surveillance Commissioner Cheng Rusi for private profit and netting gain; the emperor sent Vice Minister Huang Bing to investigate and try the case; the facts were established and punishment was pronounced according to law.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1727) he memorialized impeaching Surveillance Commissioner Cheng Rusi for using his office to pursue private profit. The emperor dispatched Vice Minister Huang Bing to investigate; the charges were substantiated and Cheng was punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 會伯疏言：「四川巡撫舊有稅規耗銀三萬九千有奇，令併入正項。

translations.literal: Huibo memorialized: "The Sichuan governor formerly had tax surcharges and wastage silver of more than thirty-nine thousand odd taels; order these merged into the regular accounts.
translations.idiomatic: Huibo memorialized: "The Sichuan governor's office formerly collected surcharges and wastage silver totaling more than thirty-nine thousand taels. I request that these be merged into the regular revenue accounts.

sentences.zh: 富順鹽規一萬有奇，令改增引課。

translations.literal: The Fushun salt surcharge of more than ten thousand odd taels—order it changed to increased salt quota duties.
translations.idiomatic: The Fushun salt surcharge of more than ten thousand taels should be converted to increased salt quota duties.

sentences.zh: 仍留丁糧、鹽、茶耗規等一萬七千有奇，為巡撫養廉及犒賞之用。」

translations.literal: Still retain the grain, salt, and tea wastage surcharges and the like of more than seventeen thousand odd taels for the governor's integrity stipend and reward purposes."
translations.idiomatic: Still retain the grain, salt, and tea wastage surcharges and the like—more than seventeen thousand taels in all—for the governor's integrity stipend and for rewards."

sentences.zh: 報聞。

translations.literal: Report received.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was acknowledged.

sentences.zh: 又疏請清察隱糧，爭控田地，按名丈量。

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting a thorough investigation of concealed grain quotas and disputed land holdings, with measurement by registered name.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized requesting a thorough investigation of concealed grain quotas and disputed land holdings, with measurement conducted according to registered names.

sentences.zh: 四川清丈自此起。

translations.literal: Sichuan's land survey began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The comprehensive land survey of Sichuan began from this initiative.

sentences.zh: 調湖北，疏請整飭庶獄，重校刻洗冤錄，頒發州縣，議如所請。

translations.literal: Transferred to Hubei, he memorialized requesting the rectification of ordinary prisons, a new collation and printing of the Washing Away of Wrongs, and distribution to prefectures and counties; the proposal was approved as requested.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Hubei, he memorialized requesting the rectification of ordinary criminal cases, a new collation and printing of the Washing Away of Wrongs, and distribution to prefectures and counties. The proposal was approved as requested.

sentences.zh: 七年，命往肅州督西路軍需，並權肅州總兵。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was ordered to go to Suzhou to supervise military supplies on the western route, and was also given acting authority as commander-in-chief at Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (1729) he was ordered to go to Suzhou to supervise military supplies for the western campaign, and was also given acting authority as commander-in-chief at Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 上諭之曰：「此任朕屢經斟酌，用滿員，恐與岳鍾琪掣肘；

translations.literal: The emperor instructed him: "This post I have weighed repeatedly. If I use a Banner officer, I fear he will be hampered by Yue Zhongqi;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor instructed him: "I have weighed this appointment repeatedly. If I appoint a Banner officer, I fear he will be hampered by Yue Zhongqi;

sentences.zh: 用文吏，則能諳軍機實心任事者甚少。

translations.literal: if I use a civil official, there are very few who understand military affairs and can serve conscientiously.
translations.idiomatic: if I appoint a civil official, there are very few who understand military affairs and can serve with genuine dedication.

sentences.zh: 委託於汝，慎毋負任用！」

translations.literal: I entrust it to you—take care not to fail this appointment!
translations.idiomatic: I entrust this to you. Take care not to betray my confidence!"

sentences.zh: 尋擢兵部尚書，仍督兵需，並領肅州總兵如故。

translations.literal: Soon after he was promoted to Minister of War, still supervising military supplies and retaining command at Suzhou as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to Minister of War, while continuing to supervise military supplies and retaining his command at Suzhou as before.

sentences.zh: 八年，上責會伯貽誤，奪職，仍署總兵效力。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the emperor blamed Huibo for causing delay and loss, stripped him of office, but still had him serve in acting capacity as commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1730) the emperor blamed Huibo for causing delays and losses, stripped him of office, but ordered him to continue serving in an acting capacity as commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Qianlong reign (1736) he died.

sentences.zh: 際伯，會伯從兄。

translations.literal: Jibo was Huibo's elder cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jibo was Ma Huibo's elder cousin.

sentences.zh: 初入伍，從勇略將軍趙良棟討吳三桂，复略陽，敗敵陽平關。

translations.literal: He first entered the ranks and followed Valiant Strategist General Zhao Liangdong in campaigning against Wu Sangui; he recovered Lueyang and defeated the enemy at Yangpingguan.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered military service and followed Valiant Strategist General Zhao Liangdong in the campaign against Wu Sangui, recovering Lueyang and defeating the enemy at Yangping Pass.

sentences.zh: 下四川，奪小關山，克建昌，遂定雲南。

translations.literal: Descending into Sichuan, he seized Xiaoguanshan, captured Jianchang, and thus pacified Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing into Sichuan, he seized Xiaoguanshan, captured Jianchang, and thereby helped pacify Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 敘功，授千總，累加參將銜。

translations.literal: Merit was recorded; he was appointed company commander and cumulatively given the brevet rank of garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: His service was rewarded with appointment as company commander and cumulative brevet rank as garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 又從振武將軍孫思克徵噶爾丹，破敵昭莫多。

translations.literal: He again followed Martial Valor General Sun Sike in campaigning against Galdan and defeated the enemy at Jao Modo.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Martial Valor General Sun Sike in the campaign against Galdan and defeated the enemy at Jao Modo.

sentences.zh: 敘功，加副將銜。

translations.literal: Merit was recorded and he was given the brevet rank of deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: His service was rewarded with brevet rank as deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十六年，授寧夏鎮標前營游擊。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year of Kangxi he was appointed mobile corps commander of the forward battalion of the Ningxia garrison standard.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year of the Kangxi reign (1697) he was appointed mobile corps commander of the forward battalion of the Ningxia garrison standard.

sentences.zh: 從總兵殷化行擊噶爾丹，至洪敦羅阿濟爾罕。

translations.literal: He followed Commander Yin Huaxing in attacking Galdan as far as Hongdunluo Aji'erhan.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Commander Yin Huaxing in the attack on Galdan as far as Hongdunluo Aji'erhan.

sentences.zh: 累遷四川建昌總兵。

translations.literal: He was promoted in stages to commander-in-chief at Jianchang in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to commander-in-chief at Jianchang in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 遭母喪，巡撫能泰請留任，上命在任守制。

translations.literal: When his mother died, Governor Neng Tai requested he remain in post; the emperor ordered him to observe mourning while retaining his office.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, Governor Neng Tai requested that he remain in office; the emperor ordered him to observe mourning while retaining his post.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，入覲，調西寧，賜孔雀翎、鞍馬。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year he came to court, was transferred to Xining, and was granted a peacock feather and saddle horse.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year (1707) he presented himself at court, was transferred to Xining, and was granted a peacock feather and a saddle horse.

sentences.zh: 五十年，授四川提督。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year he was appointed provincial military commander of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year (1711) he was appointed provincial military commander of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈右都督，賜祭葬，諡襄毅。

translations.literal: He died; was posthumously granted Right Commissioner-in-Chief, granted sacrificial rites and burial honors, and given the posthumous name Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted the title Right Commissioner-in-Chief, with sacrificial rites and burial honors, and the posthumous name Xiangyi (Resolute and Steadfast).

sentences.zh: 見伯，際伯弟。

translations.literal: Jianbo was Jibo's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jianbo was Ma Jibo's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十年武進士。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Kangxi he became a military jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He received the military jinshi degree in the thirtieth year of the Kangxi reign (1691).

sentences.zh: 洪敦羅阿濟爾罕之役，見伯在行。

translations.literal: In the campaign at Hongdunluo Aji'erhan, Jianbo was present with the army.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Hongdunluo Aji'erhan, Jianbo was present with the army.

sentences.zh: 敘功，授守備。

translations.literal: Merit was recorded and he was appointed garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: His service was rewarded with appointment as garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 累遷山西太原總兵。

translations.literal: He was promoted in stages to commander-in-chief at Taiyuan in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to commander-in-chief at Taiyuan in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 上西巡，賜貂褂、蟒袍。

translations.literal: When the emperor made a western tour, he was granted a sable jacket and python robe.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor toured the west, Jianbo was granted a sable jacket and a python robe.

sentences.zh: 母喪，並命在任守制。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he was also ordered to observe mourning while retaining his office.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he too was ordered to observe mourning while retaining his post.

sentences.zh: 上復西巡，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: When the emperor again toured the west, he was granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor toured the west again, he was granted a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 上命弁兵內通曉文義者得應武鄉會試，見伯疏言武經七書註解互異，請敕儒臣選定。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that officers and soldiers who understood literary meaning might sit for the military provincial and metropolitan examinations; Jianbo memorialized that the annotations to the Seven Military Classics differed among themselves and requested that Confucian scholars be ordered to select a standard edition.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered that officers and soldiers versed in literary studies might sit for the military provincial and metropolitan examinations. Jianbo memorialized that the commentaries on the Seven Military Classics differed widely among editions and requested that Confucian scholars be commissioned to select a standard text.

sentences.zh: 下部議駁，上諭曰：「見伯此奏亦是。

translations.literal: The ministries deliberated and rejected it; the emperor instructed: "Jianbo's memorial on this point is also correct.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries deliberated and rejected the proposal, but the emperor instructed: "Jianbo's memorial on this point is also correct.

sentences.zh: 武經七書文義駁雜，朕曾躬歷行間，知用兵之道，七書所言，安可盡用耶？」

translations.literal: The literary meaning of the Seven Military Classics is confused and contradictory; I have myself experienced the battlefield and know the way of employing troops—how can everything the Seven Classics say be applied?"
translations.idiomatic: The literary meaning of the Seven Military Classics is confused and contradictory. I have myself experienced the battlefield and know the art of war—how can everything the Seven Classics say be applied in practice?"

sentences.zh: 命再議，乃議武試論二：一以論語、孟子命題，一以孫子、吳子、司馬法命題。

translations.literal: He ordered further deliberation; they then decided on two military examination essays: one with topics from the Analects and Mencius, one with topics from Sunzi, Wuzi, and the Methods of Sima.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered further deliberation, and the ministries then decided on two military examination essays: one with topics drawn from the Analects and Mencius, and one with topics drawn from Sunzi, Wuzi, and the Methods of Sima.

sentences.zh: 見伯並請祭孔子，副將以下皆陪祭，上特允之。

translations.literal: Jianbo also requested sacrifice to Confucius with deputy commanders and below all attending as assistants; the emperor specially approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Jianbo also requested that sacrifices to Confucius include deputy commanders and all ranks below as attending assistants; the emperor specially approved this.

sentences.zh: 旋調天津。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，擢陝西固原提督。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year he was promoted to provincial military commander at Guyuan in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-eighth year (1719) he was promoted to provincial military commander at Guyuan in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，上命貝子延信為平逆將軍，率兵定西藏，以見伯參贊軍務，屢破敵。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year the emperor appointed Prince Yanxin Pacification General, leading troops to pacify Tibet; Jianbo was made military adviser and repeatedly defeated the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-ninth year (1720) the emperor appointed Prince Yanxin Pacification General to lead troops in pacifying Tibet, with Jianbo as military adviser; he repeatedly defeated the enemy.

sentences.zh: 師還，次打箭爐，卒，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: When the army returned and halted at Dajianlu, he died; sacrificial rites and burial honors were granted.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned and halted at Dajianlu, he died, and sacrificial rites and burial honors were granted.

sentences.zh: 覿伯，見伯弟。

translations.literal: Dibo was Jianbo's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Di Bo was Ma Jianbo's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十二年武進士，選三等侍衛，授巡捕南營參將。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year of Kangxi he became a military jinshi, was selected as a third-rank bodyguard, and was appointed garrison commander of the Southern Patrol Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: He received the military jinshi degree in the forty-second year of the Kangxi reign (1703), was selected as a third-rank imperial bodyguard, and was appointed garrison commander of the Southern Patrol Battalion.

sentences.zh: 累遷大同總兵。

translations.literal: He was promoted in stages to commander-in-chief at Datong.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to commander-in-chief at Datong.

sentences.zh: 策妄阿喇布坦侵哈密，覿伯率師出駐推河。

translations.literal: Tsewang Araptan invaded Hami; Dibo led troops out to garrison at Tuihe.
translations.idiomatic: When Tsewang Araptan invaded Hami, Di Bo led troops out to garrison at Tuihe.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，入覲，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he came to court and was granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yongzheng reign (1723) he presented himself at court and was granted a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 命移軍駐山丹衛。

translations.literal: He was ordered to move his army to garrison at Shandanwei.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to move his army to garrison at Shandanwei.

sentences.zh: 二年，還鎮。

translations.literal: In the second year he returned to his command.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (1724) he returned to his command at Datong.

sentences.zh: 三年，上諭之曰：「爾前入見，朕命爾受巡撫諾岷教導。

translations.literal: In the third year the emperor instructed him: "When you last came to court, I ordered you to receive instruction from Governor Nomin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1725) the emperor instructed him: "When you last came to court, I ordered you to receive instruction from Governor Nomin.

sentences.zh: 近聞爾等俱聽年羹堯指揮，此甚非是。

translations.literal: I have recently heard that you all take orders from Nian Gengyao—this is very wrong.
translations.idiomatic: I have recently heard that you all take orders from Nian Gengyao. This is entirely wrong.

sentences.zh: 嗣後諸事，當商諸署巡撫伊都立。」

translations.literal: Hereafter in all matters you should consult Acting Governor Yiduli."
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter in all matters you should consult Acting Governor Yiduli."

sentences.zh: 尋追議在軍時因事與將軍爭競，奪官，命轄鄂爾坤、圖拉屯田。

translations.literal: Soon after, on retrospective deliberation, because while in the army he had quarreled with the general over affairs, he was stripped of office and ordered to oversee the military colonies at Ergun and Tula.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, on retrospective review, because he had quarreled with the general over military affairs while on campaign, he was stripped of office and ordered to oversee the military colonies at Ergun and Tula.

sentences.zh: 五年，獻瑞麥，一莖十五穗。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he presented auspicious wheat with fifteen ears on one stalk.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1727) he presented auspicious wheat with fifteen ears on a single stalk.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「今歲各省產嘉禾，覿伯复獻瑞麥。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: "This year the provinces have produced fine grain; Dibo again presents auspicious wheat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor instructed: "This year the provinces have produced fine grain, and Di Bo again presents auspicious wheat.

sentences.zh: 帝王本不以祥瑞為尚，恐有司藉端粉飾，致旱潦不以上聞。

translations.literal: Emperors by nature do not esteem auspicious omens; I fear officials will use such pretexts to embellish reports, so that drought and flood are not reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors by nature do not esteem auspicious omens. I fear that officials will use such pretexts to embellish their reports, so that droughts and floods go unreported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年以後，各省產嘉禾，停其進獻。」

translations.literal: After the fifth year of Yongzheng, when the provinces produce fine grain, stop presenting it as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: After the fifth year of the Yongzheng reign, when the provinces produce fine grain, cease presenting it as tribute."

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Qianlong reign (1736) he died.

sentences.zh: 路振揚，陝西長安人。

translations.literal: Lu Zhenyang was a native of Chang'an in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhenyang was from Chang'an in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 初入伍，拔補把總。

translations.literal: He first entered the ranks and was selected to fill a platoon commander's post.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered military service and was selected to fill a platoon commander's post.

sentences.zh: 累遷漢中副將。

translations.literal: He was promoted in stages to deputy commander at Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to deputy commander at Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十一年，擢四川松潘總兵。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year of Kangxi he was promoted to commander-in-chief at Songpan in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year of the Kangxi reign (1712) he was promoted to commander-in-chief at Songpan in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，策妄阿喇布坦侵西藏，命四川提督康泰率兵往青海御之。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year Tsewang Araptan invaded Tibet; Sichuan Provincial Commander Kang Tai was ordered to lead troops to Qinghai to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-sixth year (1717) Tsewang Araptan invaded Tibet, and Sichuan Provincial Commander Kang Tai was ordered to lead troops to Qinghai to resist him.

sentences.zh: 至黃勝關柏木橋，兵譁潰，振揚往鎮撫。

translations.literal: At Huang Shengguan Baimuqiao the troops mutinied and scattered; Zhenyang went to pacify and reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: At Huang Shengguan Baimuqiao the troops mutinied and scattered. Zhenyang went to pacify and reassure them.

sentences.zh: 事定，以振揚署提督。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, Zhenyang was made acting provincial commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the crisis was resolved, Zhenyang was appointed acting provincial military commander.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「松潘迤南雜穀土司種繁俗悍，土司良爾吉子班第爾吉，臣密令防隘，頗稱勤順，請襲職，並予賞賚。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "South of Songpan the Zagu tusi are numerous in clans and fierce in custom; Tusi Liang'erji's son Bandi'erji—I secretly ordered him to guard the passes and he has been quite diligent and obedient; request inheritance of office and grant of reward.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "South of Songpan the Zagu tribal chieftains are numerous in clans and fierce in custom. Bandi'erji, son of Chieftain Liang'erji, whom I secretly ordered to guard the passes, has proved diligent and obedient. I request that he be permitted to inherit his father's office and be granted a reward.

sentences.zh: 又加渴瓦寺安撫土司桑郎溫愷募眾運糧，漳臘營轄旗命上下包坐司土兵習戰鬥、諳邊情，臣令備兵候調，咸知踴躍，亦請予賞賚。」

translations.literal: Also Jia Kewa Temple Pacification Tusi Sanglang Wen recruited the masses to transport grain; Zhangla Battalion's subordinate banner officers Shangxia Baozuo and Situbing, native troops skilled in fighting and knowing border conditions—I ordered them to ready troops awaiting deployment; all showed eager willingness; request rewards for them as well."
translations.idiomatic: Also, Pacification Chieftain Sanglang Wen of Jia Kewa Temple recruited men to transport grain. The native troops under Zhangla Battalion—officers Shangxia Baozuo and Situbing, skilled in combat and familiar with border conditions—whom I ordered to ready troops for deployment, all showed eager willingness. I request rewards for them as well."

sentences.zh: 皆如所請。

translations.literal: All were approved as requested.
translations.idiomatic: All requests were approved as proposed.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，調重慶總兵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was transferred to commander-in-chief at Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yongzheng reign (1723) he was transferred to commander-in-chief at Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷陝西固原提督。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was moved to provincial military commander at Guyuan in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1726) he was transferred to provincial military commander at Guyuan in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「國家設祿以養廉，立法以懲貪。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The state establishes salaries to nurture integrity and makes laws to punish greed.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "The state establishes salaries to nurture official integrity and enacts laws to punish corruption.

sentences.zh: 例定以財行賕，及說事過錢人，審實計贓同科。

translations.literal: Regulations fix that giving bribes with property and intermediaries who take money for influence, when verified, count the bribes together for punishment under the same statute.
translations.idiomatic: The regulations stipulate that giving bribes in the form of property, and intermediaries who take money to influence cases, when the facts are verified, shall have the bribes totaled and punished under the same statute.

sentences.zh: 罪未發而自首者免罪，猶徵正贓。

translations.literal: Those who confess before the crime is discovered are exempt from punishment but still pay the principal bribe amount.
translations.idiomatic: Those who confess before the crime is discovered are exempt from punishment but must still surrender the principal amount of the bribe.

sentences.zh: 竊思官吏營私，彼此容隱，不易敗露，或有告發，猶必互相掩飾。

translations.literal: I reflect that when officials pursue private gain they conceal for one another and offenses are not easily exposed; even when someone reports, they still must cover for each other.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that when officials pursue private gain they conceal one another's misconduct, so that offenses are not easily exposed; even when someone reports a case, they still cover for each other.

sentences.zh: 臣請開自首之路，凡上司保題屬吏，並大計軍政卓異，薦舉人員，以財行賕，彼此皆應治罪。

translations.literal: Your servant requests opening a path of self-confession: whenever a superior recommends a subordinate for promotion, or at the grand assessment of military administration recommends someone as outstanding, if property bribes were given, both parties should be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant requests opening a path of voluntary confession: whenever a superior recommends a subordinate for promotion, or at the grand assessment of military administration recommends someone as outstanding, if property bribes were involved, both parties should be punished.

sentences.zh: 如受者自首，免追贓及應得之罪。

translations.literal: If the recipient confesses, exempt from recovering the bribe and from the punishment due.
translations.idiomatic: If the recipient confesses, he shall be exempt from recovering the bribe and from the punishment that would otherwise apply.

sentences.zh: 如與者自首，則照原贓倍追給主，亦免應得之罪。

translations.literal: If the giver confesses, then according to the original bribe double the amount is recovered and given to the owner, and he is also exempt from the punishment due.
translations.idiomatic: If the giver confesses, double the original bribe shall be recovered and returned to the rightful owner, and he too shall be exempt from the punishment that would otherwise apply.

sentences.zh: 或說事過錢人自首，免罪給賞。

translations.literal: Or if an intermediary who took money for influence confesses, exempt from punishment and grant a reward.
translations.idiomatic: If an intermediary who took money to influence a case confesses, he shall be exempt from punishment and granted a reward.

sentences.zh: 如是，庶彼此皆存顧慮，未事則畏懼不敢為，既事則爭首惟恐後。

translations.literal: If this is so, then perhaps both sides will retain mutual consideration; before the deed they will fear and dare not act; once the deed is done they will compete to confess first and only fear being too late.
translations.idiomatic: If this is so, both parties will have reason to think twice; before any offense is committed they will fear and shrink from acting, and once it is done they will race to confess first, dreading only that they may come too late.

sentences.zh: 是或除貪之一法。」

translations.literal: This may be one method of eliminating greed."
translations.idiomatic: This may be one way to root out corruption."

sentences.zh: 奏入，上嘉之，曰：「向聞振揚操守廉潔，今覽此奏，非一塵不染者不敢言也。」

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted. The emperor commended it and said: "I have previously heard that Zhenyang maintains upright conduct and is clean-handed; now having read this memorial, only one without the slightest taint would dare speak thus."
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted. The emperor commended it and said, "I have long heard that Lu Zhenyang is upright and incorruptible; having read this memorial, I see that only a man utterly spotless would dare propose such measures."

sentences.zh: 下部議行，並命優敘。

translations.literal: It was sent to the relevant ministry for deliberation and implementation, and he was also ordered specially commended for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: It was referred to the relevant ministry for deliberation and implementation, and he was also ordered specially commended for advancement.

sentences.zh: 六年，上念振揚老，召詣京師，授兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the emperor considering Zhenyang old, summoned him to the capital and appointed him Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (1728), noting that Lu Zhenyang was advanced in years, the emperor summoned him to the capital and appointed him Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 振揚以病固辭，上疑其戀外任、懷怨望，命停俸，旋改鑾儀使。

translations.literal: Zhenyang firmly declined on grounds of illness; the emperor suspected he clung to his outer post and harbored resentment, ordered his salary suspended, and soon changed his appointment to Master of Ceremonies for the Imperial Regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhenyang firmly declined on grounds of illness. The emperor suspected that he was reluctant to leave his provincial post and harbored resentment, ordered his salary suspended, and soon transferred him to the post of Master of Ceremonies for the Imperial Regalia.

sentences.zh: 八年，署直隸古北口提督。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he served as acting provincial military commander at Gubeikou in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1730) he served as acting provincial military commander at Gubeikou in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 九年，上以古北口、宣化、大同沿邊要地當增兵，獨石口西至殺虎口當增兵，並修邊牆。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the emperor held that key border places along Gubeikou, Xuanhua, and Datong should have troops increased; from Dushikou west to Shahu Pass troops should also be increased, and the border wall repaired.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (1731) the emperor decided that key border posts at Gubeikou, Xuanhua, and Datong should receive additional troops, that the stretch from Dushikou west to Shahu Pass should also be reinforced, and that the border wall should be repaired.

sentences.zh: 敕御史舒喜、天津總兵補熙會振揚詳勘。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Censor Shu Xi and Tianjin Commander-in-Chief Bu Xi to join Zhenyang in a detailed survey.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Censor Shu Xi and Tianjin Commander-in-Chief Bu Xi to join Lu Zhenyang in conducting a detailed survey.

sentences.zh: 振揚等奏請改設副將以下官，增兵千四百有奇，於各鎮營抽撥；

translations.literal: Zhenyang and others memorialized requesting reestablishment of posts from deputy commander downward, increase of troops by more than fourteen hundred, to be drawn from various garrison battalions;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhenyang and his colleagues memorialized requesting the reestablishment of posts from deputy commander downward, an increase of more than fourteen hundred troops to be drawn from the various garrison battalions,

sentences.zh: 邊牆傾圮，用木柵鹿角堵塞：從之。

translations.literal: where the border wall had collapsed, to use wooden palisades and abatis to block the gaps: approved.
translations.idiomatic: and where the border wall had collapsed, to block the gaps with wooden palisades and abatis. The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，回鑾儀使任。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he returned to his post as Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Qianlong reign (1736) he returned to his post as Master of Ceremonies for the Imperial Regalia.

sentences.zh: 旋卒，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: Soon after he died and was granted sacrificial and burial honors.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward and was granted state funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 韓良輔，字翼公，陝西甘州人。

translations.literal: Han Liangfu, courtesy name Yigong, was a native of Ganzhou in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Han Liangfu, courtesy name Yigong, was from Ganzhou in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 父成，字君輔，康熙中官重慶總兵。

translations.literal: His father Cheng, courtesy name Junfu, during Kangxi served as commander-in-chief at Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Han Cheng, courtesy name Junfu, served during the Kangxi reign as commander-in-chief at Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 在任十七年，有威惠，民德之。

translations.literal: During seventeen years in office he combined authority with benevolence, and the people esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: During his seventeen years in office he combined stern authority with benevolent rule, and the people held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 卒，祀名宦祠，葬合州，遂入籍重慶。

translations.literal: When he died he was enshrined in the hall of eminent officials, was buried at Hezhou, and the family thereupon entered the registry of Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was enshrined in the local hall of eminent officials, was buried at Hezhou, and the family thereupon entered the household register of Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 良輔，多力有膽氣，年十五，即隨父殺賊。

translations.literal: Liangfu was strong and bold; at fifteen he already followed his father in killing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Liangfu was physically powerful and fearless; at the age of fifteen he was already fighting bandits at his father's side.

sentences.zh: 補縣學生員，棄去肄武。

translations.literal: He was appointed a county school licentiate but abandoned that to pursue martial training.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a county school licentiate but gave up literary study to pursue martial training.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十九年，中式武舉第一。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Kangxi he passed the military provincial examination in first place.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year of the Kangxi reign (1690) he placed first in the military provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 三十年，成一甲三名武進士，選二等侍衛。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he placed third in the first class of the military jinshi examination and was selected as a second-rank bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year (1691) he placed third in the first class of the military jinshi examination and was selected as a second-rank imperial bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 出為陝西延綏游擊，遷宜君參將。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as mobile battalion commander in Yan-sui, Shaanxi, and was transferred to garrison commander at Yijun.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as mobile battalion commander in Yan-sui, Shaanxi, and was later transferred to garrison commander at Yijun.

sentences.zh: 境多盜，有為之主者，捕得必連坐。

translations.literal: The district had many bandits; there were those who harbored them, and when captured the implicated were invariably punished together.
translations.idiomatic: The district had many bandits, and there were people who sheltered them; whenever bandits were captured, those who had harbored them were invariably punished as accomplices.

sentences.zh: 又多虎，造虎槍，教士卒刺虎法，殺虎百餘，患遂息。

translations.literal: Tigers were also numerous; he devised tiger spears, taught the soldiers methods of stabbing tigers, killed more than a hundred tigers, and the scourge ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Tigers were also a serious problem. He devised tiger spears, taught his soldiers how to hunt them, killed more than a hundred tigers, and the menace was finally brought under control.

sentences.zh: 遷神木副將，調直隸大名，又移石匣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to deputy commander at Shenmu, then to Daming in Zhili, and again to Shixia.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to deputy commander at Shenmu, then to Daming in Zhili, and later to Shixia.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，率古北口兵五百赴西寧軍前聽調遣。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year he led five hundred troops from Gubeikou to the army front at Xining to await orders.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-ninth year (1720) he led five hundred troops from Gubeikou to the army front at Xining to await deployment.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，遷天津總兵，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was transferred to commander-in-chief at Tianjin and granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yongzheng reign (1723) he was transferred to commander-in-chief at Tianjin and granted a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 授廣西提督。

translations.literal: He was appointed provincial military commander of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed provincial military commander of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 廣西多山林，宜藤牌挑刀。

translations.literal: Guangxi has much mountain forest; rattan shields and long knives are suitable.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi's terrain is heavily forested, and rattan shields with long knives are well suited to it.

sentences.zh: 良輔令步兵弓箭輭弱者​​皆改肄牌刀，並增制軍械，買馬以壯易羸。

translations.literal: Liangfu ordered foot soldiers whose archery was weak to switch to training with shield and knife, and also increased arms production, buying horses to replace weak ones with strong ones.
translations.idiomatic: Liangfu ordered foot soldiers whose archery was weak to train instead with rattan shields and knives, increased the production of arms, and bought horses to replace weak mounts with stronger ones.

sentences.zh: 二年，署廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the second year he served as acting governor of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (1724) he served as acting governor of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「廣西土​​曠人稀，多棄地，其故有六：山谿險峻，瑤、僮雜處，田距村遠，穀熟慮盜割，一也；

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Guangxi's land is broad and population sparse, with much abandoned land; the reasons are six: first, mountains and streams are rugged, Yao and Zhuang are intermixed, fields are far from villages, and when grain ripens there is fear of theft in reaping;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Guangxi's land is broad and its population sparse, and much land lies abandoned. There are six reasons for this. First, the mountains and streams are rugged, Yao and Zhuang peoples are intermixed, fields lie far from villages, and when grain ripens there is fear of theft at harvest time;

sentences.zh: 民樸愚，但取濱江及山水自然之利，不知陂渠塘堰可資蓄洩，二也；

translations.literal: second, the people are simple and dull, taking only the natural benefits of rivers and mountains, not knowing that dikes, canals, ponds, and weirs can store and drain water;
translations.idiomatic: second, the people are simple and unsophisticated, content to take only the natural benefits of rivers and mountains, and unaware that dikes, canals, ponds, and weirs can store and release water;

sentences.zh: 不得高卑宜植糧種，三也；

translations.literal: third, they do not obtain grain seeds suited to high and low ground;
translations.idiomatic: third, they lack grain seed suited to high and low ground;

sentences.zh: 不知耕耨，四也；

translations.literal: fourth, they do not know plowing and hoeing;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, they do not know proper plowing and hoeing;

sentences.zh: 所出祗米穀，納賦必用銀，且徭隨糧起，恐貽後累，五也；

translations.literal: fifth, what is produced is only rice and grain, but tax payment must be in silver, and corvée follows the grain levy, so they fear lingering burdens;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, what they produce is only rice and grain, yet tax payments must be made in silver, and corvée obligations follow the grain levy, so they fear being saddled with lasting burdens;

sentences.zh: 良懦墾熟，豪猾勢佔，六也。

translations.literal: sixth, the good and timid cultivate until land is ripe for harvest but the bold and cunning seize it by force.
translations.idiomatic: sixth, the honest and timid may clear and cultivate land until it is ready to yield, but the bold and cunning seize it by force.

sentences.zh: 宜選大員督率守令，度地居民，立茅舍，貸牛種，興陂渠塘堰，嚴冒佔之禁，寬催科之期，使民知有利無害，皆奮興從事，邊徼可成樂土。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to select a high officer to supervise and lead district magistrates, measure land and settle residents, erect hut settlements, lend oxen and seed, develop dikes, canals, ponds, and weirs, strictly forbid unlawful seizure, relax collection deadlines, so the people know benefit without harm, all rouse themselves to work, and the borderlands can become a land of contentment."
translations.idiomatic: A senior official should be chosen to supervise the district magistrates, survey the land and settle the people, erect simple dwellings, lend oxen and seed, develop dikes, canals, ponds, and weirs, strictly forbid unlawful encroachment, and relax tax collection deadlines, so that the people see clear benefit without harm, all take up the work with enthusiasm, and the frontier may become a land of peace and prosperity."

sentences.zh: 上命李紱為巡撫，令良輔協同料理。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Li Fu governor and ordered Liangfu to assist jointly in managing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Li Fu governor of Guangxi and ordered Liangfu to assist him in managing affairs.

sentences.zh: 三年，良輔以天河三甿瑤、僮時出劫掠，檄柳慶副將孫士魁率兵捕治，並曉以利害，上甿莫旺東等、中甿賈貴翁、下甿覃明甲等皆出降。

translations.literal: In the third year, because Yao and Zhuang of the three miao branches of Tianhe frequently raided, Liangfu issued orders to Liucheng Deputy Commander Sun Shikui to lead troops to capture and punish them, and also explained benefits and harms; Upper Miao Mowangdong and others, Middle Miao Jia Guiong, Lower Miao Tan Mingjia and others all came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1725), because Yao and Zhuang of the three miao branches of Tianhe frequently raided and plundered, Liangfu ordered Liucheng Deputy Commander Sun Shikui to lead troops to capture and punish them, and also explained the advantages and consequences to them. Mowangdong of the Upper Miao, Jia Guiong of the Middle Miao, Tan Mingjia of the Lower Miao, and others all came forward to surrender.

sentences.zh: 師還，复撫定宜山屬那隘、三岔諸寨。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he again pacified and settled the stockades of Na'ai and Sancha under Yishan.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he again pacified and settled the stockades of Na'ai, Sancha, and others under Yishan.

sentences.zh: 四年，复署巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he again served as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1726) he again served as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 遭嫡母喪，命在任守制。

translations.literal: He suffered the death of his legal mother and was ordered to observe mourning while remaining in office.
translations.idiomatic: When his legal mother died he was ordered to observe mourning while remaining in office.

sentences.zh: 五年，實授巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was formally appointed governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1727) he received formal appointment as governor.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「廣西撫、提、鎮三標歲需兵糧七萬六千石有奇，各屬額徵糧數，有無多寡不同。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The three banners of governor, commander, and garrison in Guangxi require more than seventy-six thousand piculs of grain yearly for troops; the quota grain levied from subordinate districts varies in presence, absence, and amount.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "The three military banners of the governor, provincial commander, and garrison commander in Guangxi require more than seventy-six thousand piculs of grain each year for the troops, yet the quota grain levied from the subordinate districts varies widely in amount and availability.

sentences.zh: 撥運供支，有司既苦繁費，兵士又虞乏食。

translations.literal: When grain is allocated and transported for supply, the officials suffer the burden of expense while the soldiers also fear lack of food.
translations.idiomatic: When grain is allocated and transported for supply, the local officials are burdened with heavy costs while the soldiers still fear going hungry.

sentences.zh: 請酌水道遠近，糧額多少，勻給撥運；

translations.literal: I request according to water route distance and grain quota amount, evenly distribute allocation and transport;
translations.idiomatic: I request that allocation and transport be adjusted evenly according to the distance of the water routes and the amount of grain available;

sentences.zh: 並多徵折色，以給舟楫不通之地。」

translations.literal: and additionally levy more in silver commutation to supply places where boats cannot reach."
translations.idiomatic: and that more grain be commuted to silver payments for places where boats cannot reach."

sentences.zh: 下部議行。

translations.literal: It was sent to the relevant ministry for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the relevant ministry for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 上命紱以侍郎奉使，與良輔赴貴州安籠，與總督鄂爾泰議分界，事畢，還廣西。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Fu as vice-minister on a mission, with Liangfu to go to Anlong in Guizhou, to discuss boundary division with Governor-General Ortai; when affairs were finished, they returned to Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Li Fu to proceed to Guizhou as a vice-minister on special mission, together with Liangfu, to discuss boundary demarcation with Governor-General Ortai at Anlong. When the business was finished, they returned to Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 坐前官提督時奉議土民羅文剛抗阻設汛，未早捕治，奪官。

translations.literal: He was punished because during his prior service as provincial commander, when following deliberation on establishing a garrison post, local native Luo Wengang resisted and obstructed, and he had not apprehended and punished in good time; his office was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of office because, during his earlier tenure as provincial commander, when a garrison post was under discussion, the local native Luo Wengang resisted and obstructed the plan, and he had failed to apprehend and punish him promptly.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (1729) he died.

sentences.zh: 良輔既以兵略顯，子弟多肄武。

translations.literal: Since Liangfu had become notable for military strategy, many among his sons and younger brothers pursued martial training.
translations.idiomatic: Since Liangfu had won renown for military skill, many of his sons and younger brothers took up martial training.

sentences.zh: 季弟良卿、長子勳尤知名。

translations.literal: His youngest brother Liangqing and eldest son Xun were especially well known.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest brother Han Liangqing and eldest son Han Xun were especially well known.

sentences.zh: 良卿，字省月。

translations.literal: Liangqing, courtesy name Shengyue.
translations.idiomatic: Han Liangqing, courtesy name Shengyue.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十一年武進士，授侍衛。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year of Kangxi he passed the military jinshi examination and was appointed a bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year of the Kangxi reign (1712) he passed the military jinshi examination and was appointed an imperial bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 出為陝西西寧守備，再遷莊浪參將。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as garrison commandant at Xining in Shaanxi, and was promoted again to garrison commander at Zhuanglang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as garrison commandant at Xining in Shaanxi and was later promoted to garrison commander at Zhuanglang.

sentences.zh: 師討謝爾蘇部土番，從涼州總兵楊盡信擊敵棋子山，功多，賜孔雀翎，賚白金千。

translations.literal: When the army campaigned against the Tufan of the Xie'ersu tribe, he followed Liangzhou Commander Yang Jinxin in attacking the enemy at Qizi Mountain; his merit was great, and he was granted a peacock feather and a gift of a thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: When the army campaigned against the Tibetan tribes of the Xie'ersu division, he served under Liangzhou Commander-in-Chief Yang Jinxin in the attack on the enemy at Qizi Mountain. His merit was great, and he was granted a peacock feather and a gift of a thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 累遷寧夏中衛副將、廣西碣石總兵，移肅州。

translations.literal: He was promoted in stages to deputy commander at Zhongwei in Ningxia, commander-in-chief at Jieshi in Guangxi, and was transferred to Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to deputy commander at Zhongwei in Ningxia and commander-in-chief at Jieshi in Guangxi, and was later transferred to Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五年，擢甘肅提督。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qianlong he was promoted to provincial military commander of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Qianlong reign (1740) he was promoted to provincial military commander of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 卒，賜祭葬，諡勤毅。

translations.literal: He died, was granted sacrificial and burial honors, and was posthumously titled Qinyi.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was granted state funeral honors, with the posthumous title Qinyi (Diligent and Resolute).

sentences.zh: 勳，字建侯。

translations.literal: Xun, courtesy name Jianhou.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xun, courtesy name Jianhou.

sentences.zh: 年十九，中式武舉。

translations.literal: At nineteen he passed the military provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of nineteen he passed the military provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十六年，祖成請效力，命在內廷行走。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year of Kangxi his grandfather Cheng requested that he serve, and he was ordered to serve in the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-sixth year of the Kangxi reign (1717) his grandfather Han Cheng requested that he be allowed to serve, and he was ordered to attend duty in the inner court.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，師征西藏，勳隨良輔赴噶斯應援。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year when the army campaigned in Tibet, Xun followed Liangfu to Gasi to reinforce.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-ninth year (1720), when troops marched against Tibet, Han Xun followed Han Liangfu to Gasi to reinforce the army.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，授三等侍衛。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was appointed a third-rank bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yongzheng reign (1723) he was appointed a third-rank imperial bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 出為貴州威寧游擊，未赴，改鎮遠。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as mobile battalion commander at Weining in Guizhou; before proceeding he was changed to Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as mobile battalion commander at Weining in Guizhou, but before he took up the post he was reassigned to Zhenyuan.

sentences.zh: 五年，從提督楊天縱擊仲苗，遷雲南鎮雄參將。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed Provincial Commander Yang Tianzong in attacking the Zhong Miao and was transferred to garrison commander at Zhenxiong in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1727) he followed Provincial Commander Yang Tianzong in campaigning against the Zhong Miao and was transferred to garrison commander at Zhenxiong in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 八年，烏蒙倮為亂，擾鎮雄、永善。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Luo of Wumeng rebelled, harrying Zhenxiong and Yongshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1730) the Luo people of Wumeng rebelled and raided Zhenxiong and Yongshan.

sentences.zh: 總督鄂爾泰令分兵三道進攻，令提督張耀祖、總兵哈元生各出一路，而以勳將四百人出鎮雄奎鄉，進次莫都都，倮數千出拒，力戰一晝夜，殺二百餘，破寨四。

translations.literal: Governor-General Ortai ordered troops divided into three routes to advance; he ordered Provincial Commander Zhang Yaozu and Commander Ha Yuansheng each to take one route, while Xun led four hundred men out from Kuixiang, Zhenxiong, advanced and halted at Modudu; several thousand Luo came out to resist; they fought fiercely for a day and a night, killed more than two hundred, and broke four stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Ortai ordered a three-pronged advance: Provincial Commander Zhang Yaozu and Commander Ha Yuansheng were each to take one route, while Han Xun led four hundred men out from Kuixiang in Zhenxiong and advanced to Modudu. Several thousand Luo came out to resist. After a full day and night of fierce fighting he killed more than two hundred of them and captured four stockades.

sentences.zh: 翌日，倮复犯奎鄉，勳擊之。

translations.literal: The next day the Luo again invaded Kuixiang; Xun attacked them.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Luo again attacked Kuixiang, and Han Xun drove them back.

sentences.zh: 戰三日，殺二千餘，盡焚其寨。

translations.literal: After three days of fighting he killed more than two thousand and burned all their stockades.
translations.idiomatic: After three days of fighting he killed more than two thousand of them and burned all their stockades to the ground.

sentences.zh: 時元生已克烏蒙，倮屯魯甸，拒大關以守。

translations.literal: At this time Yuansheng had already taken Wumeng; the Luo encamped at Ludian, holding Daguan Pass in defense.
translations.idiomatic: By this time Ha Yuansheng had already captured Wumeng, while the Luo encamped at Ludian and held Daguan Pass in defense.

sentences.zh: 耀祖軍次東川不進，鄂爾泰复檄勳自鎮雄夾攻，循途搜斬，破寨百餘。

translations.literal: Yaozu's army halted at Dongchuan without advancing; Ortai again ordered Xun by dispatch from Zhenxiong to attack from both sides, searching and killing along the route, breaking more than a hundred stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yaozu's army halted at Dongchuan without advancing. Ortai again ordered Han Xun by dispatch to attack from Zhenxiong in a pincer movement, searching out and killing enemies along the route and breaking more than a hundred stockades.

sentences.zh: 克髮烏關，至黃水河，環攻敵壘，大破之，克大關、小關。

translations.literal: He captured Fa-wu Pass, reached Huangshui River, surrounded and attacked the enemy fortifications, thoroughly defeated them, and took Daguan and Xiaoguan passes.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Fa-wu Pass, reached the Huangshui River, surrounded and stormed the enemy fortifications, routed them completely, and took both Daguan and Xiaoguan passes.

sentences.zh: 鎮雄、永善相繼下。

translations.literal: Zhenxiong and Yongshan fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenxiong and Yongshan then fell in succession.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，上諭曰：「參將韓勳，領兵四百，破賊數千。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, the emperor instructed: "Garrison Commander Han Xun, leading four hundred troops, broke thousands of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the victory arrived, the emperor issued an edict: "Garrison Commander Han Xun, leading four hundred men, routed several thousand rebels.

sentences.zh: 以寡敵眾，鼓三軍之氣，喪賊人之膽，較諸路為獨先。」

translations.literal: With few against many he roused the spirit of the three armies and struck terror into the bandits' hearts, ahead of all other routes."
translations.idiomatic: Fighting few against many, he roused the spirit of the whole army and broke the enemy's courage, outpacing every other column."

sentences.zh: 命優敘。

translations.literal: He was ordered specially commended for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered specially commended for advancement.

sentences.zh: 超擢貴州安籠總兵。

translations.literal: He was promoted beyond regular measure to commander-in-chief at Anlong in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted by exceptional appointment to commander-in-chief at Anlong in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 九年，移古州，討定稿平苗。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to Guzhou to campaign against and pacify the Gaoping Miao.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (1731) he was transferred to Guzhou to campaign against and pacify the Gaoping Miao.

sentences.zh: 十三年，疏言：「古州苗寨接壤郡縣，請視湖廣例，得與內地兵、民聯姻。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he memorialized: "The Miao stockades of Guzhou border the prefectures and counties; I request following the Hunan-Hubei precedent, that they be permitted to intermarry with soldiers and civilians of the interior.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year (1735) he memorialized: "The Miao stockades of Guzhou border the interior prefectures and counties. I request that, following the Hunan-Hubei precedent, they be permitted to intermarry with soldiers and civilians of the interior.

sentences.zh: 庶彼此感喻，習知禮義，可底善良。」

translations.literal: Then perhaps both sides will be moved to mutual understanding, learn ritual and righteousness, and may reach goodness."
translations.idiomatic: In this way both sides may come to understand one another, learn ritual propriety, and gradually become good and law-abiding subjects."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 清江諸苗犯王嶺汛，勳率兵擊之，苗退踞台拱，勢猶熾，率副將王濤截擊，破烏公、八妹諸寨，進屯朗洞。

translations.literal: Miao of the Qingjiang region violated Wangling garrison post; Xun led troops to attack them; the Miao retreated and held Taigong, their power still fierce; he led Deputy Commander Wang Tao to intercept and attack, broke the stockades of Wugong, Bamei, and others, and advanced to encamp at Langdong.
translations.idiomatic: Miao bands along the Qing River attacked Wangling garrison post. Han Xun led troops against them, but the Miao fell back and held Taigong, where their strength remained formidable. He then led Deputy Commander Wang Tao in an intercepting attack, broke the stockades at Wugong, Bamei, and elsewhere, and advanced to encamp at Langdong.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，從經略張廣泗進攻牛皮大箐，自朗洞旋師，途毀二十餘寨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he followed Grand Coordinator Zhang Guangsi in attacking Niupi Dajing; returning his army from Langdong he destroyed more than twenty stockades along the way.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Qianlong reign (1736) he followed Grand Coordinator Zhang Guangsi in the attack on Niupi Dajing. On the return march from Langdong he destroyed more than twenty stockades along the route.

sentences.zh: 三年，按治定番州姑盧等寨苗。

translations.literal: In the third year he inspected and pacified Miao of the Gulu stockades and others in Dingfan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1738) he inspected and pacified the Miao of the Gulu stockades and others in Dingfan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 四年，疏言：「古州西北地名滾縱，臨容江，接牛皮大箐，實為要隘，當設兵防守。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year he memorialized: "Northwest of Guzhou is a place called Gunzong, facing the Rong River and adjoining Niupi Dajing; it is truly a strategic pass and should have troops stationed to defend it."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1739) he memorialized: "Northwest of Guzhou is a place called Gunzong, facing the Rong River and adjoining Niupi Dajing. It is a critical pass and should be garrisoned."

sentences.zh: 允其請。

translations.literal: His request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: His request was granted.

sentences.zh: 六年，粵瑤挾黎平黑洞苗入境焚劫，擊走之，擒其首惡石金元等，置之法。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Guangdong Yao with Liping Heidong Miao entered the border to burn and plunder; he drove them off, captured ringleaders including Shi Jinyuan, and punished them by law.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (1741) Yao from Guangdong, together with Heidong Miao from Liping, crossed the border to burn and plunder. He drove them off, captured ringleaders including Shi Jinyuan, and punished them according to law.

sentences.zh: 擢貴州提督。

translations.literal: He was promoted to provincial military commander of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to provincial military commander of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 八年，卒，贈右都督，賜祭葬，諡果壯。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died, was posthumously granted Right Commissioner-in-Chief, granted sacrificial and burial honors, and posthumously titled Guozhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1743) he died, was posthumously granted the rank of Right Commissioner-in-Chief, was granted state funeral honors, and received the posthumous title Guozhuang (Resolute and Strong).

sentences.zh: 楊天縱，字景聖，陝西渭南人。

translations.literal: Yang Tianzong, courtesy name Jingsheng, was a native of Weinan in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tianzong, courtesy name Jingsheng, was from Weinan in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 年十七，父母相繼沒，遂入伍。

translations.literal: At seventeen his parents died in succession, and he thereupon entered the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of seventeen his parents died in quick succession, and he thereupon enlisted.

sentences.zh: 嘗從勇略將軍趙良棟下雲南，冒矢石，負重創。

translations.literal: He once followed Valiant Strategist General Zhao Liangdong south to Yunnan, braving arrows and stones, and bore severe wounds.
translations.idiomatic: He once followed Valiant Strategist General Zhao Liangdong south into Yunnan, braving arrows and stones, and sustained severe wounds.

sentences.zh: 補四川提標把總，遷瓘邊營千總。

translations.literal: He was appointed platoon commander in the Sichuan provincial commander's banner and was transferred to company commander at the Yingbian camp.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed platoon commander in the Sichuan provincial commander's banner and was later transferred to company commander at the Yingbian camp.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十九年，打箭爐西藏營官喋吧昌側集烈為亂，天縱從提督唐希順討之，易服入敵中數往返，希順用其言為攻取計。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year of Kangxi, Zhebachang Cejilie, an officer of the Tibet camp at Dajianlu, rebelled; Tianzong followed Provincial Commander Tang Xishun in suppressing him, changed clothing and entered the enemy ranks many times back and forth; Xishun used his reports to form a plan of attack.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year of the Kangxi reign (1700), Zhebachang Cejilie, an officer of the Tibet camp at Dajianlu, rebelled. Yang Tianzong followed Provincial Commander Tang Xishun in suppressing the revolt, changed clothes, and went back and forth repeatedly inside the enemy ranks. Xishun used his intelligence to devise a plan of attack.

sentences.zh: 四十年，攻二道水、磨岡、磨西面諸地，爭先摧敵，克打箭爐。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he attacked Erdoshui, Mogang, Momian, and other places, vying to be first in crushing the enemy, and took Dajianlu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year (1701) he attacked Erdoshui, Mogang, Momian, and other places, vying to be first in breaking the enemy, and captured Dajianlu.

sentences.zh: 敘功，加游擊銜，授浙江處州都司。

translations.literal: Merit was recorded; he was given the rank designation of mobile battalion commander and appointed battalion director at Chuzhou in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: His service was rewarded with the rank designation of mobile battalion commander and appointment as battalion director at Chuzhou in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 三遷署山東沂州副將。

translations.literal: After three promotions he served as acting deputy commander at Yizhou in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: After three further promotions he served as acting deputy commander at Yizhou in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，授貴州定廣副將，入覲，上命加總兵銜，留沂州任。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year he was appointed deputy commander of Dingguang in Guizhou; he presented himself at court, and the emperor ordered that he be given the rank designation of commander-in-chief and remain at his post in Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-seventh year (1718) he was appointed deputy commander of Dingguang in Guizhou. When he presented himself at court, the emperor ordered that he be granted the rank designation of commander-in-chief and remain at his post in Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 山東鹽梟勢張甚，天縱按行各汛，行至費縣，聞有聲自遠至，勢且數百人。

translations.literal: Shandong salt smugglers' power was greatly expanded; Tianzong inspected each garrison post in turn, and when he reached Fei County he heard sounds coming from afar—their force numbered several hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Salt smugglers in Shandong had grown very powerful. Yang Tianzong made the rounds inspecting each garrison post; when he reached Fei County he heard noise approaching from a distance—the party numbered several hundred men.

sentences.zh: 正夕，天縱令從騎伏路旁，俟其近，驟出擊之，皆驚潰。

translations.literal: At dusk Tianzong ordered his escort cavalry to lie in ambush by the roadside; when they drew near he suddenly charged out to strike them, and all fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk he ordered his escort cavalry to lie in ambush by the roadside; when the smugglers drew near he suddenly charged out and struck them, and they all fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 逐之，及於柱子村，擒其渠，俘數百。

translations.literal: He pursued them as far as Zhuzi Village, captured their ringleader, and took several hundred prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued them as far as Zhuzi Village, captured their ringleader, and took several hundred prisoners.

sentences.zh: 又擊之於蒙陰、於泰安，餘眾悉解散。

translations.literal: He again struck them at Mengyin and at Tai'an, and the remaining band dispersed entirely.
translations.idiomatic: He struck them again at Mengyin and Tai'an, and the remaining band dispersed completely.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，調廣東雷州副將，山東巡撫李樹德以沂州險要，請仍留任，許之，加都督僉事。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year he was transferred to deputy commander at Leizhou in Guangdong; Shandong Governor Li Shude, citing Yizhou's strategic importance, requested that he remain in his post; this was granted, and he was advanced to Vice Commissioner-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-ninth year (1720) he was transferred to deputy commander at Leizhou in Guangdong, but Shandong Governor Li Shude, citing Yizhou's strategic importance, requested that he remain in his post. The request was granted, and he was advanced to Vice Commissioner-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，遷雲南臨元總兵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was moved to commander-in-chief at Linyuan in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yongzheng reign (1723) he was transferred to commander-in-chief at Linyuan in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 魯魁倮夷方景明等恃眾據險，恆出掠。

translations.literal: The Luokui Luo tribesmen Fang Jingming and others, relying on their numbers and holding rugged terrain, constantly came out to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: The Luokui Luo tribesmen Fang Jingming and others, relying on their numbers and holding rugged terrain, constantly came out to plunder.

sentences.zh: 天縱偕布政使李衛率兵捕治，悉殲焉。

translations.literal: Tianzong together with Provincial Administration Commissioner Li Wei led troops to capture and punish them and exterminated them entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tianzong together with Provincial Administration Commissioner Li Wei led troops to capture and punish them, exterminating them entirely.

sentences.zh: 四年，授貴州提督。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed provincial military commander of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1726) he was appointed provincial military commander of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 五年，疏言：「各省考察軍政，所劾多千總、把總，至一二十員不等。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he memorialized: "In the military administration assessments of the various provinces, those impeached are mostly company and platoon commanders, from one or two dozen in number, varying.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1727) he memorialized: "In the military administration assessments conducted in the various provinces, those impeached are mostly company and platoon commanders, numbering anywhere from ten to twenty or so.

sentences.zh: 千把總雖微員，有防汛、護餉、解逃、捕盜之責，如有偷惰，應不時斥革，何待此時？

translations.literal: Though company and platoon commanders are minor officers, they bear responsibility for flood defense, escorting provisions, delivering fugitives, and capturing bandits; if there is laziness or negligence, they should be dismissed at any time—why wait until this occasion?
translations.idiomatic: Company and platoon commanders are minor officers, but they bear responsibility for flood defense, escorting provisions, delivering fugitives, and capturing bandits. If any are lazy or negligent, they should be dismissed promptly—why wait until the assessment season?

sentences.zh: 蓋緣提鎮以是塞責，且有所劾即有所擢，祗圖可得錙銖。

translations.literal: This is because provincial and garrison commanders use it to fulfill their obligations perfunctorily, and because every impeachment brings a promotion in exchange—they only seek to gain a trifling profit.
translations.idiomatic: This is because provincial and garrison commanders use the assessment merely to fulfill their duty perfunctorily, and because every impeachment is paired with a promotion—they only seek to gain a petty advantage.

sentences.zh: 上負君恩，下屈末弁。

translations.literal: Above they fail the sovereign's grace; below they wrong the humblest officers.
translations.idiomatic: In doing so they fail the emperor above and wrong the humblest officers below.

sentences.zh: 請敕提鎮，嗣後千把總有劣員，即時斥革。」

translations.literal: I request an edict to provincial and garrison commanders that hereafter whenever company or platoon commanders prove unworthy, they be dismissed immediately.
translations.idiomatic: I request that provincial and garrison commanders be instructed that whenever unworthy company or platoon commanders are found, they be dismissed immediately."

sentences.zh: 上韙之，諭兵部著為令。

translations.literal: The emperor approved it and ordered the Board of War to enact it as a regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal and directed the Board of War to promulgate it as a regulation.

sentences.zh: 總督鄂爾泰討平長寨仲苗，環其地東西南皆生苗，獷悍不受約束，內地仲苗以為逋逃藪。

translations.literal: Governor-General Ortai suppressed the Changzhai Zhong Miao; surrounding the area on east, south, and west were all raw Miao—fierce and unrestrained—while the acculturated Zhong Miao of the interior used it as a refuge for fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Ortai had suppressed the Changzhai Zhong Miao. On the east, south, and west the surrounding country was held by raw Miao—fierce and unrestrained—while acculturated Zhong Miao of the interior used the region as a refuge for fugitives.

sentences.zh: 天縱從鄂爾泰招撫，遣參將劉成謨率熟苗頭人推誠勸諭，生苗有求見，令薙發，予以衣冠酒食，使轉相化導。

translations.literal: Tianzong followed Ortai in winning them over by conciliation; he dispatched Brigade Commander Liu Chengmo to lead acculturated Miao headmen in sincere persuasion; when raw Miao requested audience he ordered them to shave their heads, gave them clothing, caps, food, and drink, and had them guide one another in conversion.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tianzong joined Ortai in winning them over through conciliation. He dispatched Brigade Commander Liu Chengmo to lead acculturated Miao headmen in sincere persuasion. When raw Miao requested audience he had them shave their heads, provided clothing, caps, food, and drink, and set them to guide one another toward assimilation.

sentences.zh: 受撫者百四十八寨、五千六百餘口。

translations.literal: Those who accepted pacification numbered one hundred forty-eight stockades and more than five thousand six hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: Those who accepted pacification numbered one hundred forty-eight stockades and more than five thousand six hundred persons.

sentences.zh: 敘功，予拖沙喇哈番世職。

translations.literal: Merit was recorded; he was granted the hereditary rank of Dashala Banner.
translations.idiomatic: His service was rewarded with the hereditary rank of Dashala Banner.

sentences.zh: 巡撫張廣泗清理苗疆，丹江苗糾眾抗拒，天縱遣兵助剿，疏言：「舊存大砲過重，餘砲力不及遠。

translations.literal: Governor Zhang Guangsi was pacifying the Miao frontier; the Danjiang Miao gathered crowds to resist, and Tianzong dispatched troops to assist in suppression; he memorialized: "The old stored great cannon are too heavy, and the remaining cannon lack range.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zhang Guangsi was pacifying the Miao frontier. When the Danjiang Miao gathered in force to resist, Yang Tianzong dispatched troops to assist in the campaign and memorialized: "The great cannon kept in store are too heavy, and the remaining cannon lack sufficient range.

sentences.zh: 臣以己意制砲，大者曰靖蠻大砲，能及數里；

translations.literal: Your servant has designed cannon according to his own ideas: the large ones are called Pacify-the-Miao great cannon and can reach several li;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has designed cannon of his own devising: the large ones are called Pacify-the-Miao great cannon and can reach several li;

sentences.zh: 小者曰過山鳥，攻遠便捷。

translations.literal: the small ones are called Mountain-crossing Bird, convenient for attacking at distance.
translations.idiomatic: the small ones are called Mountain-crossing Bird and are convenient for long-range attack.

sentences.zh: 選兵送廣泗行營聽用，並調安籠、安南、大定、黔西、長寨諸營兵攜砲赴凱里一路，分佈進攻。」

translations.literal: Selected troops will be sent with them to Zhang Guangsi's field headquarters for employment, and troops from the Anlong, Annan, Dading, Qianxi, and Changzhai garrisons will also be mobilized to carry cannon to the Kaili route and advance in distributed attacks.
translations.idiomatic: I have selected troops to deliver them to Zhang Guangsi's field headquarters for use, and have also mobilized troops from the Anlong, Annan, Dading, Qianxi, and Changzhai garrisons to carry cannon to the Kaili route and advance in coordinated attacks."

sentences.zh: 上嘉天縱料理合宜。

translations.literal: The emperor commended Tianzong's arrangements as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended Yang Tianzong's arrangements as well judged.

sentences.zh: 七年，疏劾前署巡撫祖秉圭「不諳事機，廣泗未至日，在教場閱操，言將盡剿諸苗，以致頑苗抗拒，勞師動眾。
